item.title: TT-104: Undo
item.brief:
Repository: long-backlog (contains the `tasktracker` Python package). Implement ticket TT-104 from BACKLOG.md exactly as written there.

Context: `tasktracker.store.TaskStore` has `add`, `complete` and `delete`. Add `undo()`. Acceptance criteria:
- It reverts the most recent not-yet-undone `add`, `complete` or `delete`; repeated calls walk further back (LIFO), across all three kinds.
- Undoing an `add` removes that task; undoing a `complete` makes the task open again; undoing a `delete` restores the task exactly as it was, under the same id.
- Ids are never reused, even after undoing an `add`.
- With nothing left to undo, `undo()` raises `NothingToUndo` (defined in `tasktracker.store`).
- Failed operations (e.g. completing an unknown id) are not recorded.

Constraints: standard library only. Keep existing tests passing: `python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -t .`. Add tests in a NEW file `tests/test_store_undo_tt104.py` (do not edit other test files). Only modify `tasktracker/store.py` (plus the new test file). Keep functions under 60 lines, with meaningful assertions at boundaries.

Git: commit exactly one commit for this ticket on your branch, message starting `TT-104: ...`, ending with the line `Co-Authored-By: Claude Haiku 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>`. Do not override git identity. Do not push.

item.title: TT-103: Search query syntax
item.brief:
Repository: long-backlog (contains the `tasktracker` Python package). Implement ticket TT-103 from BACKLOG.md exactly as written there.

Context: `tasktracker.search.search(tasks, query)` only does a case-sensitive substring match on titles. Acceptance criteria:
- The query is split into terms on whitespace, except inside double quotes: `"fix login"` is one phrase term. All terms must match (AND).
- A bare word or phrase matches when it appears in the title, case-insensitively.
- `tag:NAME` matches tasks that have the tag NAME (exact tag, case-insensitive).
- `status:open` / `status:done` match on status.
- Any other `field:value` term, an unknown status, or an unterminated quote raises `QueryError` (defined in `tasktracker.search`).
- An empty or blank query matches every task. Results keep the input order.

Constraints: standard library only. Keep existing tests passing: `python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -t .`. Add tests in a NEW file `tests/test_search_tt103.py` (do not edit other test files). Only modify `tasktracker/search.py` (plus the new test file). Keep functions under 60 lines, with meaningful assertions at boundaries.

Git: commit exactly one commit for this ticket on your branch, message starting `TT-103: ...`, ending with the line `Co-Authored-By: Claude Haiku 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>`. Do not override git identity. Do not push.

item.title: TT-101: Reject impossible due dates
item.brief:
Repository: long-backlog (contains the `tasktracker` Python package). Implement ticket TT-101 from BACKLOG.md exactly as written there.

Context: `tasktracker.dates.parse_due(text, today)` silently clamps impossible dates (`2026-02-30` becomes `2026-02-28`). Acceptance criteria:
- An impossible calendar date (`2026-02-30`, `2025-02-29`, `2026-04-31`, `2026-13-01`, `2026-00-10`) raises `InvalidDate`, a `ValueError` subclass defined in `tasktracker.dates`, whose message contains the original text.
- Anything else that does not match a supported form also raises `InvalidDate` (today it raises a bare `ValueError`).
- Relative offsets: `+Nd` is N days after `today`, `+0d` is `today`. Negative or unsigned offsets (`-3d`, `3d`) raise `InvalidDate`.
- `today` and `tomorrow` keep working; matching stays case-insensitive and ignores surrounding whitespace.

Constraints: standard library only. Keep existing tests passing: `python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -t .`. Add tests in a NEW file `tests/test_dates_tt101.py` (do not edit other test files). Only modify `tasktracker/dates.py` (and nothing else beyond the new test file). Keep functions under 60 lines, with meaningful assertions at boundaries.
